points.text: 1/sqrt(k) scaling only relevant for k<C*; beyond it trivially covered, not stated
Upper bound vacuous when C* eps_RM^2 >= k, common for hard problems
'Minimax optimal' and 'optimal scaling with N' overstated; N requirement lacks matching lower bound
Unique optimal response with reward 1 is a strong assumption
Theory ignores answer clustering used in experiments; on-policy error/coverage far from practice
eps_opt is free additive term making Omega(eps_opt) lower bound near-definitional
alpha requires unknown per-prompt C*; no estimation procedure; experiments use fixed alpha
Scaling-monotonicity definition does not imply non-degradation with N as claimed
Negative results for majority vote and BoN rest on single constructed instances
BoN k-scaling analysis incomplete; only conjectured not to match BoM
Technical novelty modest; standard proof tools and lower-bound construction
Proof of Thm 6.1 not verifiable; appendix proof typos need cleanup
No confidence intervals, seeds or resampling; AIME24 only 30 problems
alpha tuned per setting, no sensitivity analysis, unclear if tuned on test
'Consistently outperforms' overstated; BoM only matches baselines for larger k
Missing baselines: weighted majority vote, sum/max reward aggregation, pessimistic/smoothed BoN
Majority voting's low accuracy wrongly presented as confirming worst-case theorem
Attribution of BoN degradation to reward over-optimisation not tested
Narrow test: k<=10, few benchmarks, one reward model
Practical relevance of verifier-free Pass@k submission setting unclear
Claimed cost savings in reward evaluations not measured
No discussion of cases with fewer than k distinct answers
Backwards-reading sentence in Section 3 and several typos
Table 1 mixes worst-case lower bounds with upper bounds
Uniqueness-of-optimum assumption restrictive; bounds rely on it
BoM threshold depends on unknown C*; no estimator or misspecification analysis
Empirical scope narrow: only math/verifier-style datasets
Negative results are worst-case pathological instances; instance-dependent bounds preferable
Guarantee requires alpha tied to pi_ref(y*) and per-prompt N threshold; no practical estimation
Experiments lack explanation of alpha choice and ablation over alpha
Dependence on N missing in Theorems 5.1 and 6.1
Upper and lower bounds do not depend on N, missing compute-regret trade-off
Theorem 5.1 does not cover regime k <~ N <~ C*
Scaling with response alphabet size unclear
Algorithm requires knowledge of C* and lower bound on eps_RM
Broader impact of Pass@k inference problem unclear
Experiments do not show benefit of scaling monotonicity as N grows
More intuition needed for coverage constant and assumptions
Reasons for alpha choices per N unexplained; accuracy vs alpha not shown
Relation to Aminian et al. BoN regret upper bound not discussed
No empirical or conceptual comparison to InfAlign
No comparison to Soft-BoN theoretically or empirically
Theorem 4.2 asymptotic constant regret needs elaboration
Unclear whether reward function is calibrated
'Mathematical equivalence' criterion for answers undefined
